regions.text: 抽象前普遍性に誤られた墜間にとつて偶然性が意味を有たぬと同様に、範を科學に取る合理形式的倫理説にとつても偶然を容れる場所はないであらう。

quote.translation: Just as contingency has no meaning for a science misled by abstract universality, so a rational and formal ethics that takes science as its model will have no room for chance.

regions.text: 道徳法をして例外を許さざる普遍自然法の如くにあらしめようとする倫理說は抽象的同一性を追ふことによつて「何ものをも意志しない意志に到達して實踐上の無宇宙論に陥るであらう。

quote.translation: An ethical theory that seeks to make the moral law into something like a universal law of nature admitting no exceptions will, by pursuing abstract identity, arrive at "a will that wills nothing" and fall into a practical acosmism.

regions.text: 道徳の内容は現在の呈供する個然性によつて個別化されたものでなければならない。道德の課題とする實踐的普遍性は抽象的普遍性であつてはならない。偶然を契機として全置を内包的に限定する具體的普遍でなければならない。

quote.translation: The content of morality must be individualised by the contingency that the present offers, and the practical universality that morality takes as its task must not be abstract universality; it must be a concrete universal that, with chance as its moment, delimits the whole intensively.

regions.text: もしすべてを形式前同一性に單一化しようとする倫理説があるとしたならば、その抽象的普遍性に反抗して死に臨んで偽つたデスデモナのやうに低らう、ティモレオンのやうに人を殺さう、オットーのやうに自殺をしょうダビデのやうに神殿に入つて盜まう飢ゑたるが故に安息日に妻の穂を摘まう（Jacobi,Werke,IIL.1816,S37）2云ふ者があつても、その弊は人間の内奥に叫ぶ良心の聲として聽かれるであらう。

quote.translation: If there were an ethical theory that sought to unify everything into formal identity, and someone rose up against its abstract universality saying, "I will lie, as Desdemona lied when dying; I will kill, as Timoleon did; I will take my own life, as Otho did; I will enter the temple and steal, as David did; and because I am hungry I will pluck ears of grain on the Sabbath" (Jacobi, Werke III, 1816, S. 37), that voice would be heard as the voice of conscience crying out in the inmost depths of the human being.

regions.text: 偶然性の實踐内面化は具體的全體に於ける無数の部分と都分との間柄の自覺にほかならない。

quote.translation: The practical internalisation of contingency is nothing other than self-awareness of the relationships between part and part among the countless parts of a concrete whole.

The one that exists in isolation, at the instant (setsuna, 刹那) when, here or there, it unexpectedly encounters (kaikō, 邂逅) the other, must bind the whole suffering and joy of Existenz to the internalisation of the external thou into the depths of the I. Chance must be made to happen upon us (kaikō, 邂逅) as though it fell into the depths of the I. Heidegger too says that "what is called chance can befall only resoluteness, from the shared environing world" (Heidegger, Sein und Zeit, S. 300), and Jaspers that "beyond any thought that can be grasped, I experience terror in the limit situation, and so experience being one with the chance I have grasped as my own" (Jaspers, Philosophie II, S. 217).
